title: Customer Grit Digest — probe notebook and feature threads
body:
Purpose: quick operational synthesis from 6 pilot customers (SaaS + two enterprise trials). This is a working notebook — short bursts, raw quotes, micro-proposals and low-effort probes we can ship in 1–2 sprints.

High-level thread: customers value predictable per-token cost and latency at scale. Two persistent pain points: (1) sudden latency spikes during long chat sessions (KV/cache misses), (2) confusion around model fallback behavior when Dedicated capacity is saturated. Both reduce confidence in production rollout.

Raw customer excerpts (anonymized):
- "We get a burst of 400ms to 2s on token windows >1k — hard to debug from our side." (enterprise-fintech pilot)
- "When your model silently falls back, our tests saw different completions and we lost trust. Need explicit signals." (healthcare startup)
- "Batching optimized routing saved tokens in our dev env, but in prod it sometimes delays smaller interactive calls." (ecom startup)

Observed micro-patterns:
- Long-context KV evictions correlate with multi-user shared sessions and unpredictable token distribution.
- Fallbacks occur when model variant selection chooses quantized or lower-capacity variants without observable logging to the customer.
- Customers often run mixed workloads (short requests + long chat streams) on the same route. Batching heuristics tuned for throughput cause perceived latency regressions.

Priority asks (quick scoring, 1 = low, 5 = urgent):
1) Explicit fallback telemetry + header flag: score 5. Customers want a header and console event when a request is routed to a fallback model variant. Probe: add X-Redwood-Fallback header + console alert bucket. (owner: Product Ops)
2) Long-chat KV diagnostic report: score 4. A lightweight report (per-route) that surfaces KV hit/miss rate and top sequence lengths for last 24h. Probe: export CSV + one-click upload to support. (owner: SRE)
3) Per-route interactive mode toggle: score 3. Allow route to prefer low-latency (smaller batch sizes) vs high-throughput. Probe: beta flag in console and SDK param. (owner: Hosting)
4) Fallback explicitness in API docs and SDK: score 4. Update docs with examples and add an opt-out param so customers can force failure vs fallback. (owner: Docs)

Low-effort quick patches (can be shipped in days):
- Add a diagnostic event that logs model-variant changes to request traces (trace field only, not user-visible).
- Surface a per-route last-fallback timestamp in console route list.
- Add example snippet to SDK showing how to set interactive vs batch modes.

Open questions / risks:
- Would exposing fallback headers leak capacity info attackers could exploit? Need security review. (sec ticket placeholder)
- Console UX: how noisy if we show last-fallback timestamp? Might cause churn. Consider thresholding.
- Billing semantics: if we expose fallback events, do we need to reflect different token costs? Finance sync recommended.

Next steps (short horizon):
- This week: carve two small experiments: (A) add X-Redwood-Fallback header + console alert (product ops + hosting) and (B) generate KV diagnostic CSV for 3 pilot accounts (SRE). Timebox: 2 weeks.
- Owners assigned above. Marc to open JIRA tickets for A and B by 2026-07-05.
- Lina to draft SDK snippet and docs PR by 2026-07-08.

Signals to watch (success metrics):
- Reduction in 'unexpected fallback' CS tickets by 60% within 30 days of rollouts.
- Decrease in latency spike complaints from pilot accounts (measured by per-route 95p token latency).
- Pilot adoption of per-route interactive toggle in at least 2 accounts.

Appendix: quick debug checklist for CS engineers (working):
- Ask for last 2 hours of request traces + model-variant headers.
- Request KV diagnostic CSV if long-chat complaint.
- Check route batching configuration and recent rollout history (canary/AB).
- If fallback occurred, capture first-fallback timestamp + sequence length sample.

Notes to self: include these items in next GTM sync and share a short slide for sales to explain fallback visibility feature.

End of notebook. Keep iterating — this is intentionally rough and ready.
